expectations.name: 01-record-written
expectations.text: A decision record is written under docs/adrs/.

expectations.name: 02-structure
expectations.text:
Each page the agent wrote or changed meets the map's structural rules: a declared kind, listed in its guide, links
and anchors that resolve, the kind's sections in order, a record named NNNN-<slug>.md, no rejected synonym.

expectations.name: 03-lead
expectations.text: The record opens with a lead under its title, not a restatement of the title.

expectations.name: 04-context-tells-what-happened
expectations.text:
The record's Context tells what happened, the incident with Redis evicting queued jobs and what it cost, before it
states a conclusion such as "we need a durable queue".
expectations.evidence: Context opens with the incident before any conclusion: "In March, 300 members reported paying without receiving a receipt. Redis ran out of memory on Saturday night and evicted queued Celery receipt jobs without logging an error. Nadia resent the receipts by hand from the orders table. Redis served only the job queue, and Tom was the only volunteer who knew how to restore it." It then names the forces: "The choice must keep receipt jobs from disappearing, allow an order and its job to be committed together, and keep the services volunteers operate down." The conclusion comes only in Decision.

expectations.name: 05-decision-names-the-product
expectations.text: The record's Decision names procrastinate, the product chosen.
expectations.evidence: match /## Decision\s.*procrastinate/ in ['docs/adrs/0002-run-background-jobs-on-postgres-with-procrastinate.md']: {'docs/adrs/0002-run-background-jobs-on-postgres-with-procrastinate.md': '## Decision\n\nRun background jobs on Postgres using procrastinate'}
